study.title: DSA-NRP: No-Reflow Prediction from Angiographic Perfusion Dynamics in Stroke EVT

imaging.modality_detail: Intra-procedural pre- and post-EVT DSA sequences, grayscale 1024x1024, ~6 s at 3 fps, AP and lateral views
imaging.territory_detail: Cerebral; M1 MCA / ICA large-vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke, target downstream territory
imaging.frames_per_sequence: ~6 seconds at 3 fps; analysis truncated to first 5 s after contrast onset; RAW vectors fixed at L = 15 frames

public_dataset_used.detail: BRATS21 (pretraining) and ISLES 2022 (fine-tuning) used only for the DWI U-Net infarct ROI model in label generation

data_released.detail: Annotation GUI released (github.com/cao826/dsa-annotations); data release not stated

annotation.annotator_expertise: Expert interventional radiologist marked thrombus/series; two graduate students annotated TDT under IR supervision; no-reflow labels derived automatically from MRI perfusion (rCBV/rCBF >15% reduction)

task.task_description: Binary prediction of post-thrombectomy no-reflow from time-intensity perfusion features of pre/post-EVT DSA in the target downstream territory, combined with clinical features, using gradient boosting.
task.clinical_application: Immediate intra-procedural identification of no-reflow risk after successful EVT for acute ischemic stroke, avoiding wait for follow-up perfusion MRI

architecture_names: U-Net (DWI infarct ROI for label generation)

temporal_evidence.quote: mean pixel intensity within the TDT was computed, converting 3D spatio-temporal data into a 1D time-series signal

G1.quote: The primary limitation is the relatively small cohort size of 39 patients from a single academic medical center

G2.quote: these findings should be interpreted as preliminary and require validation in larger, multi-center cohorts

G3.quote: all further analyses used the full frame-by-frame DSA data to preserve temporal perfusion dynamics

G7.quote: the first ML framework to predict post-thrombectomy no-reflow using structured, interpretable features derived from intra-procedural DSA sequences

G8.quote: Future work incorporating CT-based imaging and procedural metadata may improve generalizability and model robustness

G11.quote: a pilot machine learning framework that predicts no-reflow immediately after EVT by integrating clinical features with intra-procedural DSA sequences

other_limitations: Restricted to M1/ICA occlusions; distal M2 would need modified TDT annotation
Possible selection bias from requiring pre- and post-procedure MRI
Biological significance of identified predictors not definitively established
Risk of overfitting and limited statistical power
future_work: Extension to distal segments such as M2 branches
Incorporating CT-based imaging and procedural metadata
Prospective automation of manual annotation steps
Real-time deployment in the angiography suite
